ios.desc:
Crush big goals, conquer fears, and celebrate every breakthrough.

See Breakthrough turns goal‑setting into an adventure. Using evidence‑based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), exposure science, journaling, and game design, the app helps you face anxiety, take daily action, and watch progress in real time.

◆ HOW IT WORKS
1. Pick a goal or fear – public speaking, fitness milestone, launching a side business, and more.
2. Follow bite‑sized challenges – guided steps rooted in CBT and success psychology.
3. Capture proof – log photos, videos, or journal notes and earn XP.
4. Earn rewards – keep streaks alive and level up.
5. Grow together – join friends, coaches, or therapists in private teams and leaderboards.

◆ WHY YOU’LL LOVE IT
• Goal tracker with motivational streak counter  
• CBT‑inspired journal to reframe limiting thoughts  
• Exposure missions that shrink anxiety triggers  
• Dashboard showing mood, confidence, and momentum trends  
• Private by design – you choose public vs. private  

◆ PERFECT FOR
• Overcoming social anxiety or phobias  
• Entrepreneurs turning ideas into reality  
• Students and professionals who love gamified motivation  
• Coaches, counselors, and accountability partners  

Download today and turn daily actions into extraordinary growth.

show_hn.title: Show HN: See Breakthrough – AI-Powered Action Plans to Overcome Fears

quotes.text:
I built See Breakthrough (iOS & Android) to help people conquer fears and achieve personal goals using AI-generated action plans. Whether it’s public speaking, fitness, or any lingering phobia, the app creates step-by-step tasks, tracks progress via short video clips, and keeps you motivated with points, streaks, and leaderboards.
AI for personalized activities via native Swift/Kotlin apps.
A close friend’s severe travel phobia inspired me to build something that offers tangible, AI-guided steps—plus social accountability and gamification.
How it Works:
 1. Enter your goal/fear.
 2. Get a personalized action plan with progressively challenging tasks.
 3. Complete tasks, optionally record short videos, and earn points to climb leaderboards.

I’d love your feedback on everything from the AI approach to the user experience. If you’ve ever tried (and failed) to tackle a fear or build a new habit, I’m especially interested in what you think could be improved. Any tips, critiques, or wild ideas are welcome!

Thanks for checking it out.
